title: The best places to see stunning Draconid meteor shower in Sussex this week
excerpt: Sussex is home to some of the darkest skies in south-east England, making it an ideal place to watch this week's Draconid meteor shower.
content:
The Draconid meteor shower returns to UK skies this week, and those in Sussex are in a great position to see it.

Sussex is home to some of the darkest skies in south-east England, making it an ideal place to watch this week's Draconid meteor shower.

From the lofty heights of Ditchling Beacon to the dramatic coastline at Birling Gap, several locations across the South Downs National Park offer the dark, unobstructed skies needed to spot the fleeting streaks of light as they race across the night sky.

Here are the best places in the county to see it, and when to do so.

When to see the Draconid meteor shower in Sussex

Skygazers across Sussex are being encouraged to head out after dark to catch the cosmic display, which will be active between October 6 and 10.

It is expected to be visible across the county during its peak on October 9.

Unlike many other meteor showers that are best viewed in the early hours, the Draconids are most visible in the evening, making them more accessible to stargazers of all ages.

The shower is caused by Earth passing through debris left by comet 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, the Royal Museums Greenwich explains.

The rate of meteors during the shower's peak depends upon which part of the comet's trail the Earth's orbit intersects in any given year.

Viewing conditions are expected to be favourable this year, with the peak coinciding with dark skies and a thin crescent moon that will rise just before dawn.

Experts recommend finding a location with minimal light pollution, a clear horizon, and no direct sources of light.

There is no need for binoculars or telescopes, as the meteors are best viewed with the naked eye.

Where best to see the Draconid meteor shower in Sussex

In Sussex, the South Downs National Park offers some of the best stargazing spots, thanks to its status as an International Dark Sky Reserve.

Here are some of the best places to see the meteor shower:

Ditchling Beacon, East Sussex

Ditchling Beacon in East Sussex is one of the county’s highest points and offers panoramic views across the South Downs.

It is also a designated Dark Sky Discovery Site.

The South Downs offers some of the best stargazing spots in the country (Image: Matt Gibson/Getty Images)

Birling Gap and the Seven Sisters Coast

Birling Gap and the Seven Sisters coastline provide uninterrupted sea views to the south and benefit from very low levels of light pollution.

This National Trust site is also recognised as a Dark Sky Discovery Site.

Bignor Hill, West Sussex

Bignor Hill in West Sussex is often cited as one of the darkest locations in the region.

On clear, moonless nights, the Milky Way is sometimes visible from this spot.

Firle Beacon, East Sussex

Firle Beacon, located near Lewes, also offers excellent sightlines and is recognised as a strong location for stargazing.

Stargazers are advised to avoid looking at any bright lights so that they can fully adapt to the darkness.

Warm clothing, a blanket, and a little patience are all that’s needed to make the most of this celestial event.
